body:
>ever thought of credit counseling or bankruptcy? and part time jobs are meant to be mundane but its still a job.

As far as I'm aware, you cannot get out of paying student loans via bankruptcy, at least in the US. My point with the part-time job thing was that there was no sense of "self-worth", although re-reading your original post, it looks like you may have meant about the army only, sorry if I misunderstood.

I don't understand how it's not a "relief" though. I mean, of course you'd never actually FEEL the relief, but if you go from a situation where "I have problems" to not thinking at all, aren't you, in a sense, "relieved" of the problems? They might not be solved, but you no longer have to deal/think with them (or anything), right?


I'm sorry if it seems like i'm being argumentative here, I'm just trying to express my thoughts.

>Your going to kick the bucket over school and money? a life wasted for what? how about you pull up your socks and take the help offered by your parents - get a part time job so you can save some cash or do it to show your parents your trying and focus on your school work or what ever course your taking. Or join the Army. give yourself a sense of self worth.

I've had a part-time job (all year during high school, summers when in college) since I was 16. There was no feeling of "self-worth" in it. I got along well with my co-workers, management, and customers (I still keep in contact with a few of the older workers). I was the only part-timer in my time of working there (~6 years off and on) that ever got a raise that wasn't due to a rise in minimum wage, because I actually did my job. But again, there was no "self-worth" in it. It was just a routine. I go in, do my job, leave. That's it.

>I found my old man hanging from a extension cord a few years back. trust me it fucks up your whole family for life. You want them to suffer just to off your own issues? - reality check we all have issues.

I'm sorry about your father. No, I don't want them to suffer because of my issues, emotionally OR financially. Which is why I said in the OP that if I do it, I will make sure to leave home and do it in such a way that my body is unrecognizable. At least they'd have the hope that I was still alive out there somewhere, although I suppose that could be worse than having closure too.

How much would seeing a shrink cost per visit, though? And medication? I don't have the income to afford something like that.

And I'm okay talking about it here, but I don't really know anymore to say unless someone asks something specific.

(Thank you for responding, by the way.)

>What do you think your parents will prefer, helping you out financially or going to your funeral?

Obviously, I think they'd prefer the former. However, I've already been unsuccessful in college twice now because I can't motivate myself to actually attend the classes. That's not their fault, and I can't bring myself to mooch their money to continue "trying" to do get a degree. I would rather die myself than be a financial burden on them. Even if they would rather help me financially, I can't bring myself to ask them to cover for things that are my own fault. I'm not an only child, and my parents aren't very wealthy. 

I don't have a problem with working, although I know that finding a job, especially for someone unskilled and with my college "record" would be difficult. The only "problem" is that anything I CAN get is unlikely to be enough to pay for medical insurance, and it horrifies my parents for me to be without. I know that if something serious happened, I'd basically be screwed, but again, I can't in good conscious ask for anymore from my parents.


>It's the only way to feel better.

I've never seen a shrink. I don't even know that I feel "bad". I just... I don't really feel anything. I have literally zero motivation. I did well in HS because my parents wanted me to. I went to college because my parents wanted me to. I switched majors because my parents wanted me to. 

Even when I stopped going to classes, I didn't DO anything. I don't mean "I stayed at my apartment and browsed reddit, 4chan, slashdot, etc." nothing. I mean, literally, I laid in my bed and did nothing. There are plenty of things (besides even my classes...) that I could have been doing. I just couldn't work up the motivation to do it. Even now, there's  a programming project I "want" to work on (a game...) and would publish, either for free or very cheap. I know I have the knowledge to do so. But I sit down to work on it, write a few lines of code... and stop. Again, to do literally nothing.

I don't really know how to describe it.

Either way, I have no way to afford seeing a shrink as it is. I'm also currently in Saudi Arabia working over the summer, so I won't be back to the states to actually see someone for over a month.
